claims.text: Sainte-Chapelle is a breathtaking royal chapel on the Île de la Cité, ordered by King Saint Louis to house his collection of holy relics.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The King specifically acquired the Holy Crown of Thorns and a piece of the True Cross starting in 1239, and built this chapel as a vast glass reliquary for them.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It is considered a masterpiece of Rayonnant Gothic architecture, famous for replacing almost all of its upper stone walls with soaring stained-glass windows.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the French Revolution, the chapel was closed to worship around 1790 and lost the precious relics that were its very reason for existing.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: By 1797, the empty chapel had been converted into an archive depot for the neighbouring Palais de Justice, which even threatened its survival.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Thanks to strong public pressure, a decision was made in 1836 to save and restore the building, leading to a long and successful campaign.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, because the chapel sits inside the active Courts of Justice complex, all visitors must pass through a strict security check to enter.
claims.subject: self
